items.title: Both Charts Are Right. So Why Do They Disagree?

items.title: Four Gemini 4 Argon agents beat Minecraft without any human help
items.summary: Four AI agents running on Google's Gemini 4 Argon have beaten Minecraft for the first time without human help, slaying the Ender Dragon in a fully autonomous run. With no predefined roles or strategies, they coordinated on their own, wrote 2,783 programs, exchanged 229 chat messages, and died 605 times.

items.title: Anthropic has nearly stopped hiring junior staff because AI agents now work six times as many hours
items.summary: Anthropic is hiring fewer and fewer junior staff in technical roles. The share of junior positions among new hires dropped from 27 to 9 percent since early 2025.

items.title: Inferring the Host: A Bayesian Look at the Monty Hall Problem
items.summary: "Always switch" is true for one particular host. Watch a few episodes and you can work out which host you've got.

items.title: Anthropic gives outside AI watchdog “employee-like” access
items.summary: The outside watchdog can publish its findings without Anthropic's approval.

items.title: TinyFish Makes Search Free: What It Really Costs an AI Agent to Read the Web
items.summary: An AI agent that reads the web pays 2 kinds of cost. The first is the retrieval charge: what a search or fetch API bills per request.

items.title: A woman was arrested in Philly for blocking a delivery robot
items.summary: Carolyn Marvin was arrested and charged with disorderly conduct after blocking the path of an Uber delivery robot and refusing to get out of the way. Marvin told Philadelphia's ABC13 "I know they're taking the jobs of human delivery workers and so, I have been protesting them whenever I saw them by standing in front […]

items.title: TorchNeuron: running HF models on AWS Trainium is easier than ever
Mistral AI Releases Timestral: A 209M Forecasting Model Family That Outperforms Google’s TimesFM-3
items.summary: Mistral released Timestral, a time series foundation model family from 5M to 209M parameters. The 209M model leads GIFT-Eval, TIME and fev-bench among zero-shot models and runs on CPU.

items.title: NVIDIA Open Sources Run:ai Under Apache 2.0 for Kubernetes GPU Orchestration
items.summary: NVIDIA has released the full Run:ai GPU orchestration platform as open source under Apache 2.0. The release includes KAI Scheduler, CUDA 13.4 GPU fractioning, quota management, and a local Kind dev environment.

items.title: Disney Asked Character.AI to Go Bankrupt for a Get-Out-of-Lawsuits Card
items.summary: The entertainment giant hopes to get trust and safety tech, among other IP, from a startup whose chatbots dozens of states allege encouraged minors to self-harm and kill their parents.

items.title: AI researchers stranded Claude on a virtual desert island. It started to “play.”
items.summary: What do AI agents do if you don’t tell them to do anything? The answer looks a lot like play.

items.title: Edge AI for Smart Cities: From Insight to Cognitive Action
items.summary: This white paper explains how edge AI and physical AI help cities move beyond passive monitoring. It shows how urban infrastructure can sense, reason, and act on real-time conditions across public safety, mobility, and infrastructure management.

items.title: AI Harms and Their Technical Causes
items.summary: How technical choices can lead to safety failures, and what to do differently The post AI Harms and Their Technical Causes appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: Anthropic plans fund for workers threatened by AI, Musk counters with SpaceX shares for children
items.summary: Anthropic wants to put five percent of its shares into a new public benefit fund that will also look into direct payments to workers at risk of losing their jobs. The fund is a company-owned LLC, so Anthropic keeps control of it as a possible IPO approaches.

items.title: The neocloud shakeout is coming, and Nvidia has the most to lose
items.summary: After stock crashes and Firmus's scrapped IPO, industry executives expect only seven to ten of the hundreds of AI cloud providers to survive. CoreWeave lost a quarter of its market value, and Microsoft pulled out of a deal with Nscale for 23,000 Nvidia chips.

items.title: Democrats think cracking down on AI could give them an edge
items.summary: Democrats could win back control of Congress this November, and if they do, they'll need to decide how to approach one of the country's newest and thorniest political issues: AI. Polls predict Democrats will flip at least one chamber of Congress in the midterm elections, which would put committee leadership back in their hands.

items.title: Advancing coding in low‑resource programming languages
items.summary: Learn how OpenAI is improving ChatGPT across low-resource programming languages, with new evaluations for software engineering, SQLite, and COBOL migration.

items.title: How Many EEG Channels Do You Actually Need?
items.summary: Testing sensor reduction, feature ranking, and generalization to unseen participants The post How Many EEG Channels Do You Actually Need? appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: MiniMax Just Launched M3.1 Flash: 428B MoE Agentic Model at $0.15/M Input
items.summary: MiniMax has released M3.1 Flash, a 428B-parameter MoE model with about 23B active parameters and a 1M-token context. API pricing is $0.15/$0.60 per 1M tokens, with weights due October 23 The post MiniMax Just Launched M3.1 Flash: 428B MoE Agentic Model at $0.15/M Input appeared first on MarkTechPost .

items.title: Stripe says AI agent purchases are adding up, but it won't share the numbers
items.summary: AI agents are increasingly using Stripe's payment service Link to shop for their users, Upstarts Media reports. The article Stripe says AI agent purchases are adding up, but it won't share the numbers appeared first on The Decoder .

items.title: Inside Prometheus: Meta’s Journey to a Gigawatt-Scale Supercluster
items.summary: With the recent release of the Muse family of foundational models, we want to take you inside the infrastructure that has made it all possible. The first phase of Prometheus, our gigawatt-scale supercluster, is already complete and we’re working toward scaling it to comprise ~1 million GPUs.

items.title: A hacker broke into John Deere and SharkNinja with an army of AI agents
items.summary: A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge. Though Norforge doesn't name the targets, Reuters reports that the victims included companies like John Deere, SharkNinja, and Cummins.

items.title: Can Conformal Prediction Take You from Accurate to Reliable Machine Learning?
items.summary: ML model adoption doesn't stop with acceptance of accuracy; it starts there. The post Can Conformal Prediction Take You from Accurate to Reliable Machine Learning?

items.title: JB Pritzker thinks AI could help us live to 100 — or threaten us like nukes
items.summary: Today, I’m talking with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, who has a lot of thoughts about AI, tech, and privacy.

items.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
items.summary: Character.AI faces claims its bots encouraged minors to self-harm and kill their parents.

items.title: Two German courts now hold Google liable for what its AI overviews say
items.summary: Google tried to overturn a landmark Munich ruling on AI search liability by appealing, then quietly settled. The strategy isn't working.

items.title: Welcome to Google Gemini 4 Argon
items.summary: A million-token output window changes what you can hand a model in one go, and the benchmarks and the bill show who it actually suits. The post Welcome to Google Gemini 4 Argon appeared first on Towards Data Science .

items.title: The Thin Orchestrator: How We Made Our AI Agents More Reliable by Giving the Router Less to Do
items.summary: Sometimes, giving an AI agent all of the knowledge it needs is the wrong approach. At Meta, we’ve seen notable improvements in efficiency and accuracy by keeping the orchestration layer of our data pipeline agents deliberately thin: It routes work and enforces reliability checks, while specialized agents do the domain reasoning.

items.title: WhatsApp Help Pages Leaked Hidden Instructions for a Meta Chatbot
items.summary: Around 80 pages on WhatsApp’s website exposed instructions that were designed for its chatbot, including “WHAT NOT TO SAY.” Meta says a bug caused the issue.

items.title: GenRecs Tokenization: Transforming Ads Recommendation at Meta with Stable Model Vocabulary
items.summary: Generative Recommenders (GenRecs) represent a paradigm shift from scoring every ad to reasoning about ad content and user preferences together in order to predict the best outcome for advertisers. Leveraging the world knowledge built into LLMs makes ad matching more intelligent and precise, compounding gains for advertisers.

items.title: AI game clones are making indie developers afraid to show their work
items.summary: Delayed Steam Next Fest demo is a sign of a growing problem for indie devs.

items.title: Kling AI drops version 4.0 with stereo audio, multilingual lip sync, and a lighter Flash variant
items.summary: Kling AI has released version 4.0 of its video generator with support for clips up to 30 seconds, ten keyframe images as input, and prompt comprehension expanded to 8,000 tokens. In comparisons with Wan 3.0 and Seedance 2.5, Kling 4.0 holds its own but doesn't pull ahead, which could be an early sign that the breakneck pace of progress in AI video models is starting to level off.

items.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
items.summary: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and not-so-cautious) celebration. Cammarata’s claim is…

items.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash shows China's AI price race has no floor in sight
items.summary: MiniMax's M3.1 Flash jumps 13 points over its predecessor to 42 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, at half the cost. It also hits 73.7 percent on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding benchmark for under $0.30 per task, matching Deepseek V4.1 Flash 1017 on both performance and price.

items.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
items.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here.

items.title: OpenAI Engineer Accused of Spying on Executives Ordered to Remain in Custody
items.summary: A judge ordered Abdulrahman Alfozan to remain in custody, likening the Saudi government’s offer to secure the former OpenAI engineer’s release to a “blank check.”

items.title: Accused OpenAI spy had folder called “Saudi Gov Docs,” FBI says
items.summary: US fears Saudi government will help ex-OpenAI engineer flee spying charges.

items.title: CoreWeave’s debt is becoming the whole AI industry’s problem
items.summary: CoreWeave had a bad week last week. Its bonds slipped into distressed territory by a common definition - when investors demand 1,000 basis points more in yield than they'd get from government bonds.

items.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
items.summary: The US is building more fossil fuel infrastructure than it has in a decade while renewable energy growth slows down, a new report shows. Electricity demand is also climbing faster than it has in more than a decade with more data centers, factories, and electric vehicles plugging into the grid.

items.title: Meet Drex Max: Nace AI’s Multimodal Decision Model for Computer-Use Agents with a Score 67.59
items.summary: Nace AI released Drex Max, a multimodal decision model that reads text and screenshots and returns calibrated probabilities. Nace reports 67.59 on Decision Index 0.3.2 at $0.06 per 1M input tokens.

items.title: Inception Releases Mercury 3 Diffusion LLM at 1,068 Tokens per Second
items.summary: Inception released Mercury 3, a diffusion LLM it says runs at 1,068 tokens per second with a 1M-token context. On Inception’s own table it leads GPT-6 Luna and Claude Haiku 5.5 on 8 of 12 benchmarks.

items.title: [AINews] not much happened today
items.summary: Congrats to DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, and Mercury 3 (details below) but they’re not going to be in super wide use just yet.

items.title: Cloudflare Releases Clairic, a System One Extraction Model on Workers AI
items.summary: Cloudflare has previewed Clairic, a System One extraction model on Workers AI that returns typed values with confidence scores in one forward pass. It costs $0.10 per million input tokens and charges nothing for output.

items.title: Exa 3.0 Search API Tops Perplexity, Brave and Parallel on 8 Benchmarks
items.summary: Exa 3.0 is a search API upgrade from Exa. It adds a larger embedding model, Exa Lite at $4 per 1,000 requests, and Dynamic Highlights, and leads 8 benchmarks Exa ran itself.

items.title: A visit to Samsung’s massive new semiconductor hub
items.summary: Generative AI models run on powerful chips known as GPUs, which depend on stacks of specialized memory chips packaged with the processor. To meet growing demand for memory, Samsung is building a massive new semiconductor manufacturing complex in Pyeongtaek, South Korea.
